steps.1: Generate an app password with your email provider (IMAP must be enabled), then enter your email address and app password. Known providers are detected automatically; use the optional server settings for other providers.

troubleshooting.1: Most providers require an app password rather than your normal password.
troubleshooting.2: Use TLS for implicit TLS (usually port 993), or STARTTLS (usually port 143).
troubleshooting.3: For security, private, loopback, link-local, and otherwise non-public server addresses are rejected.

slack.description: Read messages from every channel, private channel, DM, and group DM you have access to

steps.1: Go to api.slack.com/apps and click "Create New App" → choose "From scratch". Name it "Nicx" and pick your workspace
steps.2: In the left sidebar, click "OAuth & Permissions". Scroll down to "User Token Scopes" (NOT "Bot Token Scopes"). Click "Add an OAuth Scope" and add EACH of these scopes one by one:
steps.3: channels:history • channels:read • groups:history • groups:read • im:history • im:read • mpim:history • mpim:read • users:read
steps.4: In the left sidebar, click "Install App" → click "Install to Workspace" → click "Allow". After installing, copy the "User OAuth Token" that appears (starts with xoxp-, NOT xoxb-)
steps.5: Paste the user token below. Sync indexes every channel, private channel, DM, and group DM you have access to — no need to invite anything to channels
steps.6: (Optional) Set the app icon: in the left sidebar click "Basic Information" → scroll to "Display Information" → upload the Nicx logo

steps.1: Go to notion.so/profile/integrations → click "+ New integration". Name it "Nicx", select your workspace, and click Submit
steps.2: Copy the "Internal Integration Secret" (starts with ntn_) and paste it below
steps.3: To share ALL your pages at once: open any top-level page → click "..." (top right) → "Connections" → "Add connections" → search "Nicx" → click it. This shares the page and all its sub-pages. Repeat for each top-level page, or share your entire workspace by doing this on every root page
steps.4: Tip: if you have a single top-level page that contains everything, sharing just that one page will share all nested sub-pages automatically

steps.1: Open the Granola desktop app. Click the gear icon (Settings) in the bottom-left corner, then click "API"
steps.2: Click "Generate API Key" (or copy your existing key). Paste the key below

steps.1: Open the Apple menu () → System Settings → Privacy & Security (in the left sidebar) → scroll down and click "Full Disk Access"
steps.2: Click the "+" button at the bottom of the list. Navigate to Applications → Utilities → select "Terminal.app" (or iTerm2/Warp if you use those). If you're using the desktop app, also add "Nicx.app" from Applications
steps.3: Toggle the switch ON next to each app you added. Close and reopen your terminal (or restart Nicx). iMessage data will be detected automatically — no credentials needed

steps.1: Find your vault path: open Obsidian → click the vault name in the bottom-left corner → "Manage Vaults" → look at the path shown under your vault name. On macOS this is usually ~/Documents/MyVault or ~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/MyVault
steps.2: Alternatively, open Finder → navigate to your vault folder (it contains a hidden .obsidian directory). Right-click the folder → "Copy as Pathname" to get the full path
steps.3: Paste the full path below. Nicx will index all .md files in the vault

steps.1: Go to Google Cloud Console → create a new project (or select an existing one). Give it any name (e.g. "Nicx")
steps.2: Enable the Google Drive API: click the link below, make sure your project is selected at the top, then click "Enable"
steps.3: Create OAuth credentials: go to Credentials (link below) → click "+ Create Credentials" → choose "OAuth client ID" → Application type: "Web application". Under "Authorized redirect URIs" add this server's callback (e.g. http://localhost:1313/v1/connectors/gdrive/oauth/callback — match the host/port your Nicx server is bound to) → click "Create".
steps.4: A dialog will show your Client ID and Client Secret. Copy both and paste them below, then click Connect — a Google sign-in window opens to finish authorization. (If you miss the dialog, click the download icon next to your OAuth client to see them again.)

steps.1: Go to the Azure Portal → App Registrations → click "+ New registration". Name it "Nicx", select "Accounts in this organizational directory only", and click Register
steps.2: In the left sidebar, click "API Permissions" → "Add a permission" → "Microsoft Graph" → "Delegated permissions" → search and check "Mail.Read" → click "Add permissions"
steps.3: In the left sidebar, click "Certificates & secrets" → "New client secret" → set a description and expiry → click "Add" → immediately copy the "Value" (you won't see it again)
steps.4: Go to "Overview" in the left sidebar and copy the "Application (client) ID". Paste both the Client ID and the Client Secret below

steps.1: Go to the Dropbox App Console and click "Create app". Choose "Scoped access" → "Full Dropbox" → give it a name (e.g. "Nicx") → click "Create app"
steps.2: Click the "Permissions" tab at the top. Check "files.metadata.read" and "files.content.read" → click "Submit" at the bottom to save
steps.3: Go back to the "Settings" tab. Under "OAuth 2", find "Generated access token" and click "Generate". Copy the token and paste it below

steps.1: Go to Meta for Developers → click "Create App" → choose "Business" type → fill in your app details and click "Create App"
steps.2: On the app dashboard, find "WhatsApp" and click "Set up". Follow the prompts to add a WhatsApp test number. Go to "API Setup" and copy the temporary access token
steps.3: Copy your "Phone Number ID" (shown on the API Setup page) and the access token. Paste them below separated by a colon — e.g. 123456789:EAABx...
